subject:
TTFT & streaming SLOs 

- post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@finlytics.com>, James Ortiz <james.ortiz@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs - post-call recap and next steps

Hi Anna / James -

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and streaming requirements we discussed.

Summary of requirements you called out:
- TTFT target: p95 <= 120 ms for text-generation first token under expected load.
- Concurrency: baseline 50 concurrent active requests, peak bursts to ~150 for short windows.
- Throughput: steady-state ~500 tokens/sec across the fleet for the model profile we discussed.
- Streaming: prefer Server-Sent Events (SSE) to start; WebSocket acceptable if we need bi-directional interactions.
- Chunk cadence target: client wants ~50-100 ms intervals between chunks for progressive UI render; smaller chunks OK as long as we don't hit per-chunk overheads.

Attached: ttft_requirements.xlsx (simple matrix of targets) and network-checklist.pdf (suggested NAT/TLS path). Please also share any sample streaming payloads / expected token lengths so we can run a small emulation.

Our immediate next steps (proposed):
1) You: share a sample streaming payload and your expected user-per-second curve for peak and sustained windows (file or short JSON).
2) Us (Redwood): we'll run a quick feasibility test on our Dedicated config (likely A10/80GB or H100 quantized profile) and come back with expected p50/p95 TTFT and recommended chunk-size / batching settings.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30-45m) with infra/ops - propose Tue 2026-03-10 11:00am PT - please confirm availability.

Questions we have now:
- Do you have a hard SLA for first token (e.g., required p95 <= 200ms) or is 120ms a target goal?
- Are you planning TLS termination at your edge or will Redwood terminate TLS inside the VPC?

Thanks - I'll start an internal run once we get the sample payload.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: ttft_requirements.xlsx (Excel), network-checklist.pdf (PDF)

Date: 2026-03-03T17:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs - post-call recap and next steps

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the key constraints from our side:
- Target SLA for launch: p95 TTFT <= 150 ms (120 ms is preferred but 150 ms is acceptable for go-live).
- Concurrency: 50 baseline, we expect short bursts up to 150 for up to 2 minutes.
- Streaming: SSE preferred (we already use EventSource in our client).
- Chunk cadence: goal 50-100 ms, but we can tolerate 150 ms if that materially improves cost/efficiency.

I attached a small example stream profile (finlytics_stream_profile.json) and a sample prompt set (included in the file). For payload sizes: typical prompt -> 50-150 input tokens, expected generated response 30-200 tokens.

Regarding TLS - we terminate TLS at our load balancer and will tunnel traffic to Redwood over mTLS (preferred).

Confirming availability for the deep-dive Tue 2026-03-10 11:00am PT.

Anna
Anna Li
Head of Product, Finlytics
anna.li@finlytics.com
Attachments: finlytics_stream_profile.json (JSON)

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks all - quick follow-ups from infra side before the deep-dive:

1) TLS / mTLS: fine to terminate at Finlytics LB; we recommend mTLS between LB and Redwood private endpoint. Can you share the cert rotation window and whether you support zero-downtime rotation?

2) Chunk cadence: the 50-100 ms goal is achievable but depends on useful chunk size. For most models we see diminishing returns under ~40ms due to per-chunk syscall overhead; recommend testing 50 ms and 100 ms cadence in the emulation.

3) Buffering and SSE: SSE has lower overhead than WebSocket for uni-directional streams. We'll provide recommended buffer sizes (bytes) after we run an emulation with your sample payloads.

4) Load profile: can you also share expected p95 request size (tokens) and the percent of requests that will stream vs non-stream (batch inference)? That helps us set batching windows.

Action items & schedule:
- Finlytics: share sample payloads + mTLS cert rotation spec (ASAP).
- Redwood (Rishi + infra): run emulation and report TTFT p50/p95 and recommended chunk sizes by 2026-03-06 COB.
- Tech deep-dive: Tue 2026-03-10 11:00am PT (invite to follow).

Link to deal + notes: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-5483
